selectedModel.selection_rule: highest validation ROC-AUC (4 d.p.), then lowest validation Brier

decisionThreshold.rule: maximises Youden's J (sensitivity + specificity - 1) on the validation partition

preprocessing: Read CSV as strings (blank = missing); originals never modified
Numeric: parsed as numbers, median imputation (training partition) + missing indicators, standardised
Categorical: blank -> 'MISSING' level, one-hot, levels < 1% grouped as infrequent, unseen levels ignored
No survey weights and no survey year used as predictors
CSV blanks cannot distinguish skip / refused / don't know (official codebook not available)

references.title: MathQuest | Expert Review Pack (Learner Profile & Prediction Engine - Draft for Review)
references.organization: Sri Lanka Institute of Information Technology (SLIIT)
references.limitations: Draft review pack prepared for consultation, not a completed validation record or empirically calibrated psychometric instrument. Rules represent initial hypotheses requiring iterative clinical and pedagogical refinement.

references.title: Guided Self-Management Tools for ADHD: Children 6-12 (Version 1.1)
references.organization: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School
references.limitations: Designed as clinician-guided parent/child home and school worksheets rather than automated software algorithms. The 5-minute break mentioned in homework examples is an illustrative guide, not a mandatory or universally appropriate duration for digital gaming. Cultural adaptation is required for Sri Lankan family contexts, bilingual Sinhala-English instruction, and software delivery. Does not provide automated telemetry decision thresholds.

references.title: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Treatment of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents
references.limitations: US-focused clinical and legal framework (Section 504 / IDEA regulations). Diagnostic criteria require specialist clinician evaluation across real-world home and classroom environments, precluding digital in-game diagnosis. Supports general clinical and educational principles but does not provide algorithmic decision thresholds for educational games.

references.title: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: Diagnosis and Management (NICE Guideline NG87)
references.organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (UK)
references.limitations: UK National Health Service clinical pathway context. Clinical diagnostic thresholds and medication protocols cannot be executed by an autonomous educational gaming system. Supports environmental modifications conceptually, but does not provide software telemetry thresholds.

references.title: Assisting Students Struggling with Mathematics: Intervention in the Elementary Grades (WWC 2021006)
references.organization: What Works Clearinghouse (WWC) / Institute of Education Sciences (IES), U.S. Department of Education
references.limitations: Grounded in small-group and 1:1 human teacher-led Tier 2 interventions in US elementary schools (Grades K–6). Digital adaptations must translate teacher-led practices into automated software scaffolds. While the guide strongly supports instructional strategies conceptually, it does not specify software decision thresholds (e.g., exact trial counts or error thresholds). These thresholds require expert review and contextual calibration.

recommendations.titleEn: Honour the child's quiet sound choice
recommendations.titleSi: දරුවා තෝරාගත් නිහඬ ශබ්ද මාදිලියට ගරු කිරීම
recommendations.action: Mute ambient and background sound; offer spoken prompts as optional tap-to-hear instead of automatic narration.
recommendations.why: The child chose soundMode 'quiet' while the parent setting is 'read_everything'.
recommendations.explanationEn: Your child selected quiet sound mode. Spoken guidance is set to 'tap-to-hear' so audio plays only when clicked, supporting calm focus.
recommendations.explanationSi: දරුවා නිහඬ ශබ්ද මාදිලිය තෝරාගෙන ඇත. එමනිසා අවශ්‍ය විටෙක පමණක් ක්ලික් කර ශ්‍රව්‍ය උපදෙස් ලබා ගැනීමට සකසා ඇත.

recommendations.titleEn: Visual & concrete object support: Counting & Number Sense
recommendations.action: Offer virtual counters or objects first, then pictures, then numerals for this skill.
recommendations.why: ELP-X reports skill 'number_sense' as EMERGING with sufficient evidence (4 items).
recommendations.explanationEn: The learner is developing foundational understanding. We recommend using virtual counters and pictorial models before practicing abstract numbers.
recommendations.explanationSi: මූලික සංකල්ප වර්ධනය වෙමින් පවතී. වියුක්ත සමීකරණ වලට පෙර, ගණන් කළ හැකි දෘශ්‍ය රූප ආධාරයෙන් පුහුණු වීම නිර්දේශ කෙරේ.

recommendations.explanationEn: The learner engages best when multi-step problems are divided into bite-sized milestones. Breaking goals down reduces cognitive overload and helps maintain focus.

nonClaims: Research prototype only; not a validated educational or clinical instrument.
A correct transfer response does not prove permanent or genuine learning.
The teaching phase is not claimed to cause any improvement.
Three transfer questions do not constitute a validated learning-readiness measure.
No mastery, frustration or readiness thresholds are applied.
No ADHD diagnosis, presentation or symptom change is inferred; ADHD reports and SNAP-IV are never used.
approvalsRequired: Primary mathematics educators: concept, number range, item-model cell, items, response format, Sinhala wording, session length.
Clinical supervisor: universal teaching phase, neutral feedback, breaks and help-on-request, reporting wording and audience, data minimisation.
Ethics approval and consent for research use of the recorded fields.
Component 1 sign-off before any integration into the onboarding journey (feature-flagged, separate protocol).

outcomes.description: 2 of 3 new questions answered correctly without help (chance per question 0.33; 0 helped, 0 unknown, 0 unanswered)
outcomes.interpretation: Descriptive count of new comparison questions answered correctly without help, shown beside the chance level.
